clue.text: He placed pin awkwardly for cabinet-maker

indicators.note: placed awkwardly means the letters of the three words are set down in a new, clumsy order

explanation.surface: Someone fumbles a pin while working for a furniture craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges HE PLACED PIN into the eighteenth-century furniture maker's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Chippendale was a celebrated English furniture designer, so his name stands for a maker of cabinets.

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to sing a Christmas song is to carol
to work something is to use it

explanation.surface: A performer sings while working in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Carousel is the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical of 1945.

indicators.note: poor suggests the two names are in a bad way, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A request to bury an unfortunate relative called Enid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges AUNT ENID.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to flood or swamp, which buries something under water or a mass.

clue.text: Exercise skill climbing in old city

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A traveller exercises their climbing skill amid ancient ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Petra is the ancient rock-cut Nabataean city in Jordan.

clue.text: Sonya, for example, arranged a posy

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A girl called Sonya puts together a little bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges SONYA plus EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small bunch of fragrant flowers, the same thing as a posy.

clue.text: Evangelist is bitter about the situation

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: bitter is a kind of beer, an ale
a post is a job or position, a situation

explanation.surface: A preacher is resentful about how things stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' looks like an adjective describing the evangelist, but it is the noun for a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles spread the gospel, so one of them is an evangelist in the broad sense of a preacher of it.

indicators.note: cut means the word is shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: easy can mean pleasant and relaxed, as in easy company
to nurse is to tend, so a nurse is a tender

explanation.surface: A Londoner snubs an agreeable nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks EASY to EAS. A Cockney is a working-class Londoner from the East End of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from London's East End is the classic Cockney, a working-class Londoner.

parts.note: a pen is a female swan, so her partner is the male swan

explanation.surface: A friend one writes letters to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing pen, but it is the female swan; her mate has a name of his own.
explanation.definitionFit: The male swan is the partner of the female, the pen.

clue.text: Draw back from phone in church

indicators.note: in means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to ring is to phone

explanation.surface: Someone recoils as a mobile goes off during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To cringe is to shrink back or flinch in fear or embarrassment.

clue.text: He makes tea in brass urn

parts.note: Br is taken as a short form of brass, the metal alloy
an ewer is a large jug, a vessel like an urn

explanation.surface: A tea-maker at work with a brass urn.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking BR for brass is loose: Br is really the chemical symbol for bromine.
explanation.definitionFit: To brew tea is to make it, so one who brews is a tea-maker.

clue.text: Stimulate corrosion with absorption of oxygen

indicators.note: with absorption of means one word takes in another, swallowing it inside

parts.note: rust is corrosion of iron
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: rusting is spurred on when oxygen is absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with absorption of' puts O inside RUST.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to rouse or stir someone up into action.

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free
spine means spirit or courage, backbone

explanation.surface: Collecting a duty on liquor made from timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots pine is a conifer whose timber is a common softwood.

clue.text: Learned drink produces rising air current

parts.note: to be up in a subject is to be well informed, learned in it
a draught is a drink, a long swallow

explanation.surface: A scholarly tipple gives rise to a warm breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' is the adjective (LEARN-ed), not the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: An updraught is an upward movement of air, a current that rises.

clue.text: Empty-headed dog welcomed on the golf course

indicators.note: empty-headed means the word's head, its first letter, is removed

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound

explanation.surface: A dim-witted hound is let onto the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty-headed' drops the B of BEAGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle, two strokes under par on a hole, is a score any golfer is glad to see.

clue.text: Yes! A rut formed in the creek

indicators.note: formed means made into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly notices a channel has worn into the creek bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed' rearranges YES A RUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An estuary is a tidal inlet where a river meets the sea, as a creek can be.

indicators.note: misrepresented means shown wrongly, so the letters appear in a different order

explanation.surface: A man called Don clears up a false story about a circus performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' rearranges DON CLEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fable, Androcles pulled a thorn from a lion's paw and was spared by the beast, so he tamed it by kindness.

indicators.note: a gorge is the inside of the throat, so the letters come from inside the word

explanation.surface: Ancient stories about Cheddar Gorge, the Somerset ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar Gorge is a limestone ravine in Somerset, England; here 'Gorge' takes the inside of CHEDDAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddas are medieval Icelandic collections of Norse myth and legend.

indicators.note: in means the first pieces go inside the last

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail
the men are a ship's crew

explanation.surface: A ship's company is greeted with bunting on arrival in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags' looks like bunting but means flagstones, the paving slabs.
explanation.definitionFit: Flags, or flagstones, are the paving slabs that make a footway.

clue.text: One willing to assess a hill

parts.note: to test something is to assess it
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone is prepared to survey a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willing' looks like eagerness but means making a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will, someone engaged in the act of willing.

parts.note: eccentric means odd, peculiar
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: An oddball enjoys a slight edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds can mean an advantage or edge, as in being given odds in a contest.

clue.text: Make one's home outside a US city

indicators.note: outside means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to settle is to make one's home somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone sets up home on the edge of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts SETTLE round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the largest city in Washington state in the USA.

parts.note: garb is clothing
to age is to deteriorate with time

explanation.surface: Worn-out clothes end up as junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is household waste, the refuse thrown away.

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
a head is a leader, as of a school

explanation.surface: An Indian state's chief minister is told to carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: To go ahead is to proceed or carry on with something.

clue.text: Man on racecourse brings good luck

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for a noun: the clue describes a thing that brings luck

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for male, a man
Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: A man at the races is a lucky charm.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is the racecourse in Berkshire, England, home of Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object thought to attract good fortune.

parts.note: pi is a ratio, the fixed relationship of a circle's circumference to its diameter
racy means lively and entertaining

explanation.surface: Someone finds that an affair adds spice to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relationship' looks romantic, but it is the mathematical ratio pi.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy is robbery at sea, or the unauthorised copying of others' work, both forms of theft.

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane

explanation.surface: A soldier's longtime comrade.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for a friend, used informally in English.

clue.text: A time to entertain part workers in the home

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the outer pieces take the others inside

parts.note: taken as written
men are workers, a workforce

explanation.surface: Someone sets aside time to host part-time staff at home.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a set of rooms used as a dwelling.

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is wrapped round the other

parts.note: a tack is a course of action or approach, a policy

explanation.surface: A government strategy concerns a rail route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside TACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A track is a line of rails, or more generally a path or course.

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a strumpet is a harlot, a prostitute
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A lady catches a woman of ill repute carrying a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: C for caught comes from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte is a woman's given name.

clue.text: A period with conservationists is a factor

parts.note: an age is a period of time
the NT, the National Trust, is a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: A stretch of time spent with environmental campaigners proves influential.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust preserves historic buildings and countryside in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is something that brings about an effect, a factor or cause.

indicators.note: lacks means a letter is missing from the word

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A Tory politician offers no resistance to a flirtation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' removes R from TORY.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with someone is to trifle or play with their affections.

indicators.note: troubled means stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the name with its possessive s

explanation.surface: Ted's loudspeaker is giving trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges TEDS SPEAKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed skater races on ice, an athlete in a winter sport.
